existing.note: Pressure Map not available this run

gas.note: 250,000 gas units per transaction (assumed) at 0.0012 gwei, plus Ink's L1 data fee (upper bound for a 300-byte transaction, from the OP-stack GasPriceOracle)

equities: No tokenized-equity collateral is listed on Tydro or as Nado spot at this block.

rules: Every rate is annual and not compounded (APR). Tydro publishes current rates; Nado does not, so Nado figures are observed over the stated window.
Observed rates come from the change in the protocol’s own index, multiplier or cumulative funding between two readings — what was actually paid, not a model.
Daily history uses checkpoints at 00:00 UTC; a pair counts as a day only if 20–28 h apart (a missed day is a gap, never stretched).
Funding reversal: HIGH if funding went against the position in the last 24 h or on 10+ of the last 30 days; MEDIUM on 4–9 days; else LOW.
Liquidation: the smallest adverse price move that liquidates a leg, from the protocols’ own weights and thresholds — HIGH under 20%, MEDIUM under 50%, else LOW; no borrowing = LOW.
Stablecoin: from Oracle Watch’s peg status of each stablecoin held — DEPEG/INVALID = HIGH, WARN/DIVERGENT = MEDIUM.
Oracle: the worst Oracle Watch status among the prices that decide the structure’s margin — OK = LOW, WARN/UNAVAILABLE = MEDIUM, anything worse = HIGH.
Protocol change: HIGH if a market is frozen, inactive or has borrowing off; MEDIUM if a recorded parameter change in the last 30 days touches it; else LOW.
Capacity: the room before a cap or the available liquidity binds — HIGH under $100,000, MEDIUM under $1,000,000; no readable cap = LOW (and said so).
Data: HIGH if the reading is over 3 h old or the rate can't be computed; MEDIUM if a window or input is missing.
Risk state = the worst factor. Deterministic and versioned; no model or AI decides it.
assumptions: Nado margin for a short hedging a Tydro position: 50% of the hedge.
Borrowing: 50% of what Tydro's LTV allows.
Gas: 250,000 units per transaction, plus Ink's L1 data fee upper bound when readable.
One-off costs are shown for $10,000 of capital and, for scale, as a rate if held 30 days.
Everything is before slippage, before Nado trading fees (not exposed on-chain) and at today’s rates, which change every block.

definitions.Gross: yields earned by the structure’s legs (supply, deposit, appreciation), per $1 of capital
definitions.Borrowing cost: interest paid on any borrowed leg, per $1 of capital
definitions.Funding contribution: perp funding received (positive) or paid (negative), per $1 of capital
definitions.Estimated net: gross − borrowing cost + funding; fees are separate one-off costs
definitions.Historical range: the lowest and highest daily net rate over the recorded days
